findings.title: Cleanup interval accidentally reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: Run() now ticks the background cleanup loop every 1 minute instead of every 10 minutes. Nothing in the PR description or the annotation deadlock fix calls for this, and it changes every job in this service (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, and annotations), not just annotation cleanup. clean() uses a 9-minute timeout that was paired with the 10-minute interval so one pass finished before the next tick. With a 1-minute ticker, any pass longer than a minute (likely now that each annotation batch is a separate SELECT plus DELETE, and on large tables) leaves a tick buffered, so the next pass starts immediately and cleanup runs back-to-back. That multiplies database load and can increase the write contention this change is meant to reduce. Restore the 10-minute interval unless a documented, intentional schedule change is actually wanted.

findings.title: Success-path debug logs at Error level dump every cleaned ID
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log at Error after every ID fetch and every delete (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), including batches that find nothing. These are leftover debug statements: the fetch log's err is always nil because a real error already returned, and the messages fire on the normal success path. Error-level lines are what most Grafana deployments alert on, so every cleanup cycle will raise false errors for alert, dashboard, and API annotations plus orphaned tags. Each line also includes the full ID slice and the SQL condition. Batch size is configurable and the new test uses 32767, so a single line can be megabytes, flooding log pipelines and risking dropped real errors. Remove these calls, or at most log a count at Debug without the ID list.

findings.title: SQLite IN-list is built with quadratic string concatenation
findings.body: When the database is SQLite and AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is above 999, deleteByIDs inlines IDs by repeatedly assigning values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v). Each iteration copies the whole string, so n IDs cost O(n²) allocations before the DELETE is sent. The new test sets the batch size to 32767, and orphaned-tag cleanup can emit several lists of that size; that is on the order of gigabytes of temporary strings and multi-second stalls on the cleanup goroutine, which runs the other cleanup jobs only after annotations finish. Build the list with strings.Builder (and consider chunking) so large SQLite batches stay linear.
